title: From Genes to Diets: A Critical Review of Genetic, Nutrigenomic and Epigenetic Mechanisms in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
authors: Araujo, Rafael G; Ortiz-Cruz, Gabriela; Nupo, Sunday Sedodo; Cordero, Yulianna; Cortes-Hernandez, Lauro; Teniente, Sandra Lucia
one_liner_zh: 该综述聚焦2型糖尿病的遗传、营养基因组学和表观遗传机制，虽提及转录因子和AI，但核心非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) represents over 90% of diabetes cases globally, posing a growing public health crisis with an estimated 783 million adults projected to be affected by 2045. This condition arises from a complex interplay of insulin resistance, progressive pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction, and chronic low-grade inflammation, strongly influenced by genetic predisposition, obesity, sedentary lifestyle, and poor dietary habits. While genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified key susceptibility loci, including TCF7L2, PPARG, and KCNJ11, these varian0ts explain only ~10% of T2D heritability, underscoring the critical role of gene-environment interactions. This review synthesizes current evidence on the genetic, nutrigenomic, and epigenetic mechanisms underlying T2D pathogenesis and progression. We examine how dietary components, such as flavonoids, terpenoids, alkaloids, and bioactive compounds from natural products, modulate gene expression via transcription factors and influence insulin sensitivity, oxidative stress, and inflammation. Furthermore, we explore the emerging role of epigenetic modifications, including DNA methylation, histone acetylation, and chromatin remodeling, in mediating the lasting effects of hyperglycemia and environmental factors on T2D risk. The potential of epigenetic biomarkers for early diagnosis, patient stratification, and personalized therapy is discussed. Finally, we highlight how next-generation sequencing and artificial intelligence, particularly machine learning and deep learning models, are advancing multi-omics data integration, enabling improved T2D subtype classification, prognosis prediction, and the development of precision nutrition and pharmacoepigenetic strategies.
abstract_zh: 2型糖尿病（T2D）占全球糖尿病病例的90%以上，预计到2045年将有7.83亿成年人受到影响，构成日益严重的公共卫生危机。该疾病源于胰岛素抵抗、进行性胰腺β细胞功能障碍和慢性低度炎症的复杂相互作用，并受遗传易感性、肥胖、久坐生活方式和不良饮食习惯的强烈影响。虽然全基因组关联研究（GWAS）已识别出关键易感位点，包括TCF7L2、PPARG和KCNJ11，但这些变异仅解释了T2D遗传力（heritability）的约10%，凸显了基因-环境相互作用的关键作用。本综述综合了关于T2D发病机制和进展背后的遗传、营养基因组学和表观遗传机制的现有证据。我们探讨了膳食成分，如类黄酮（flavonoids）、萜类化合物（terpenoids）、生物碱（alkaloids）及天然产物中的生物活性化合物，如何通过转录因子调节基因表达，并影响胰岛素敏感性、氧化应激和炎症。此外，我们探讨了表观遗传修饰（包括DNA甲基化、组蛋白乙酰化和染色质重塑）在介导高血糖和环境因素对T2D风险的持久影响中的新兴作用。讨论了表观遗传生物标志物在早期诊断、患者分层和个性化治疗中的潜力。最后，我们强调了下一代测序和人工智能（特别是机器学习和深度学习模型）如何推进多组学数据整合，从而改善T2D亚型分类、预后预测，并促进精准营养和药物表观遗传策略的发展。
